text: A man in a maroon colored flannel shirt, which had been made in New York for purposes of decoration, rounded a corner into the main street of Yellow Sky. <break time="0.8s" /> His boots had red tops with gilded imps on them, the kind beloved in winter by little sledding boys on the hillsides of New England. <break time="0.8s" /> He held a long, heavy, blue black revolver in each hand, and he often yelled, and these cries rang through a village that seemed to be deserted. <break time="0.8s" /> The calm adobe houses preserved their dignity, and there was no offer of fight, no offer of anything, and the man called angrily to the sky. <break time="0.8s" /> When the bartenders dog walked away growling, Scratchy fired at the ground just in front of it, and the frightened animal galloped away in terror. <break time="0.8s" /> Remembering Jack Potter, his ancient antagonist, he concluded that it would be a glad thing to go to Potters house and make him come out and fight. <break time="0.8s" /> Potters house presented the same still front as the other houses, and when Scratchy howled a challenge, it regarded him as might a great stone god. <break time="0.8s" /> He churned himself into deepest rage over the stillness of the house, fuming at it as the winter wind attacks a prairie cabin.
